reasons: POST has clear error handling and is tested.
GET has no error handling and no test for failure.

terms.meaning: A written rule that says what a request body must look like.
The library used to write and check those rules.
A number the server returns to say what happened, such as 201 for created or 404 for not found.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and runtime setting
sections.what: Loads the response helper, the input checking library, the anchor service, and its not-found error type. Sets the Node.js runtime.
sections.why: Likely reason: the server modules need the Node.js runtime.
sections.watch_out: The error type must be the same one the service throws, or the 404 branch will never run.

sections.name: anchorCreateSchema
sections.title: Anchor request rules
sections.what: Defines the rules for the POST body: a required result id, an optional signer name, and no extra fields.
sections.why: Protects the service from unexpected or malformed input.
sections.watch_out: Any new request field must be added to these rules or it will be rejected.

sections.name: GET
sections.title: List anchors handler
sections.what: Returns every anchor saved for the case in the address.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the case page show previous anchors.
sections.watch_out: No error handling here, so a service failure becomes a generic server error.

sections.name: POST
sections.title: Create anchor handler
sections.what: Checks the body, creates the anchor, and maps outcomes to 201, 400, 404, or 500 responses.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps bad input, a missing result, and an unexpected failure as separate responses.
sections.watch_out: The 500 message hides the real cause, so check server logs when debugging.

summary: Web address for listing a case's anchors and creating a new anchor from one verification result.
purpose: Lets officers lock in a verification result with a fingerprint and signer name, so it can be checked later.
why: Likely reason: an anchor gives a fixed record that can be verified after the fact.
how: GET returns the case's anchors. POST checks the body, creates the anchor through the service, and returns 201 on success. A missing result gives 404, and any other failure gives 500.
inputs: Case id in the address. For POST, a JSON body with resultId text and an optional signedBy name. Any extra fields are rejected.
outputs: JSON with a data field, or an error with code INVALID_INPUT, NOT_FOUND, or INTERNAL_ERROR.
risks: POST does not check that the case exists before creating the anchor in this file. GET has no error handling.
debug: A 400 means the body did not match the rule. A 404 means the result id is not known to the service. A 500 means something unexpected failed, so check server logs.
